name.rationale: The template's identifier. Naming is a team choice; we don't constrain resource names or references.

description.description: An optional textual description of the resource.
description.rationale: Free-text metadata for human readability. It has no effect on the resource's configuration or behavior.

node_affinity_labels.description:
Labels to use for node affinity, which will be used in
instance scheduling.
node_affinity_labels.rationale: Labels used purely for scheduling affinity between instances and nodes. This is an architectural/scheduling choice, not a security control, similar to other categorization labels.

node_type.description:
Node type to use for nodes group that are created from this template.
Only one of nodeTypeFlexibility and nodeType can be specified.
node_type.rationale: Specifies the sole-tenant node shape to reserve. This is a functional sizing choice with no universally secure value — appropriate node types vary entirely by workload.

cpu_overcommit_type.description:
CPU overcommit.
Default value is `NONE`.
Possible values are: `ENABLED`, `NONE`.
cpu_overcommit_type.rationale: Selects whether CPU can be oversubscribed on the node for cost efficiency. This is a functional/architectural cost-vs-isolation tradeoff with no single universally secure value.

region.description:
Region where nodes using the node template will be created.
If it is not provided, the provider region is used.
region.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

project.description:
The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifies which GCP project the template belongs to — a reference/identifier, not a security-configurable property.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform can destroy this template via IaC (DELETE/ABANDON/PREVENT). Maps to the prevent-destructive-loss archetype (same mechanism as force_destroy): PREVENT blocks hard-destroy of the resource, and a policy should enforce that value.

node_type_flexibility.description:
Flexible properties for the desired node type. Node groups that
use this node template will create nodes of a type that matches
these properties. Only one of nodeTypeFlexibility and nodeType can
be specified.

node_type_flexibility.cpus.description: Number of virtual CPUs to use.
node_type_flexibility.cpus.rationale: Specifies a CPU count constraint for flexible node matching — a capacity-sizing choice with no security implication.

node_type_flexibility.memory.description: Physical memory available to the node, defined in MB.
node_type_flexibility.memory.rationale: Specifies a memory constraint for flexible node matching — a capacity-sizing choice with no security implication.

server_binding.description:
The server binding policy for nodes using this template. Determines
where the nodes should restart following a maintenance event.

server_binding.type.description:
Type of server binding policy. If `RESTART_NODE_ON_ANY_SERVER`,
nodes using this template will restart on any physical server
following a maintenance event.
If `RESTART_NODE_ON_MINIMAL_SERVER`, nodes using this template
will restart on the same physical server following a maintenance
event, instead of being live migrated to or restarted on a new
physical server. This option may be useful if you are using
software licenses tied to the underlying server characteristics
such as physical sockets or cores, to avoid the need for
additional licenses when maintenance occurs. However, VMs on such
nodes will experience outages while maintenance is applied.
Possible values are: `RESTART_NODE_ON_ANY_SERVER`, `RESTART_NODE_ON_MINIMAL_SERVERS`.
server_binding.type.rationale: Selects maintenance-restart behavior (live-migrate vs. restart-in-place), typically driven by software licensing needs. This is a functional/architectural choice with no universally secure value.

accelerators.description:
List of the type and count of accelerator cards attached to the
node template

accelerators.accelerator_count.description:
The number of the guest accelerator cards exposed to this
node template.
accelerators.accelerator_count.rationale: Specifies how many accelerator (GPU) cards to attach — a capacity/performance sizing choice, not a security control.

accelerators.accelerator_type.description:
Full or partial URL of the accelerator type resource to expose
to this node template.
accelerators.accelerator_type.rationale: Specifies which accelerator (GPU) type to attach — a functional hardware choice with no universally secure value.

disks.description:
List of the type, size and count of disks attached to the
node template

disks.disk_count.description: Specifies the number of such disks.
disks.disk_count.rationale: Specifies how many local disks to attach — a capacity-sizing choice, not a security control.

disks.disk_type.description: Specifies the desired disk type on the node. This disk type must be a local storage type (e.g.: local-ssd). Note that for nodeTemplates, this should be the name of the disk type and not its URL.
disks.disk_type.rationale: Specifies the local storage type — a functional choice with no security implication.

disks.disk_size_gb.description: Specifies the size of the disk in base-2 GB.
disks.disk_size_gb.rationale: Specifies local disk size — a capacity-sizing choice with no security implication.
